newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Sihanouk denies he will enter politics.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk denies he will enter politics.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk has denied suggestions he planned to abdicate and enter politics, saying he would remain on the throne until the turn of the century if he lived that long.

Sihanouk, quoted in his monthly bulletin released on Tuesday, said he might be better off abdicating rather than running the risk of someday being deposed but added: "I cannot yet resolve myself to abdicate."

He said most people wanted him to remain as a protector of the people and constitution and guarantor of democracy. He added he believed the country would be plunged into chaos without his stabilising influence.

The 74-year-old king, who is in China receiving medical treatment for serious ailments, said if he abdicated politicians would say his action was motivated by desire to enter the political arena in a bid to seize political power.

He stressed he had "no desire, no impulse to exercise government or other power. In conclusion, barring unforeseen complications for me, I have no intention to abdicate ... before 2000, supposing that I live that long".
Some politicians have suggested Sihanouk could abdicate soon to take part in politics, as he did in 1955 after 14 years on the throne.
Cambodia is scheduled for national elections in 1998.

The royalist FUNCINPEC party won U.N.-sponsored elections of 1993, but after protests by the former communist Cambodian People's Party (CPP), the king arranged a coalition government between the two parties with himself as a monarch who rules but does not govern.
Political analysts believe co-Premier Hun Sen of the CPP fears the prospect of the immensely popular king running at the head of his own party in the next polls.
